correctness.rationale: For all positive parameters the multiplier B is positive on y>0. Direct differentiation (replayed by CHECK.py) produces the full smooth divergence and both Filippov one-sided formulas; the quadratic P(y) is nonnegative on the full domain exactly under b+2sqrt(a)>=0 and its possible zero set has area zero. The binary switch has negative normal jump; all sliding is attracting. Splitting any supposed simple periodic Jordan interior across the switch gives nonnegative orbit/sliding/interface flux but a strictly negative sum of area divergences. This contradiction is rigorous even at equality. It does not rely on numerical orbit simulations.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2023 source derives the one-sided Dulac expressions but does not supply a global no-cycle statement controlling the interface normal jump and sliding geometry, nor a monotone-activation robustness theorem. The exact switched/regularized conjunction is not an implication of its frozen-subsystem criteria. Earlier piecewise Dulac theorems inspected require weighted normal continuity/refraction and thus exclude the positive-q treatment jump. Literature and source-level mathematical comparisons identified no exact or dominating model-specific coverage. Abstract-only sources and unidentified more general criteria remain residual risks.
residual_risks: An unidentified general Bendixson--Dulac theorem for nonrefracted attracting switches might imply the discontinuous component; searched close preprints require weighted normal continuity, but a universal literature proof of novelty is impossible.
The 2021 smooth antecedent paper and the 2024 same-author weighted-switch follow-up were not fully inspected; abstract/model comparisons are suggestive, not comprehensive whole-document exclusions.

Conclusions concern the explicit model, monotone activation and piecewise-regular Jordan Filippov cycles; no claim about irregular differential-inclusion loops, nonmonotone control, or necessary oscillation boundaries.

value.rationale: The model explicitly explores treatment-induced crossing and sliding cycles. A threshold- and intensity-independent, explicit no-oscillation region for the full discontinuous model, robust to every differentiable monotone smoothing, is a motivated structural boundary of therapeutic oscillations. The example epsilon=6,beta=3/2 gives a certificate through r=(123+12sqrt(91))/50 about 4.74945, close to r=5 used in the source oscillatory illustrations; this anchors the threshold in a natural studied family without falsely calling it the actual bifurcation. No paper-sized follow-up theorem is claimed or required.
